descriptions.text: For the first several seasons of Dungeon Crawler World, all contestants started off as Primals. Primals are blank slates. You will look the same as before. You will obtain all skills associated with your current race, with the following exceptions: -1 to all base stats. All higher-tier skills are unlocked and are able to train to 20. Choosing this race unlocks multiple exclusive, earth-based classes.

beats.headline: Carl takes the empty box
beats.text: Race selection, on the way into the Over City. The preview model for this one is blank, because nobody alive knows what they looked like. Mordecai's summary: the progenitors, the first species to conquer the universe, the boogeymen of the cosmos, gone one day without a note. Taking it costs fifteen stat points against staying human: the ten a human gets, and five more. What it buys is a ceiling. Every skill trainable to twenty, and only a rare few who take it ever train one or two skills above fifteen.

beats.headline: A hunter uses the word about the AI
beats.text: Iota tells Carl the AI is starting to go primal: ignoring court orders, doing as it pleases. He says the rumour on his side is that the Mantises sold Borant a used one under the table. Carl kills him. The word stays.

beats.headline: Primal Engines, on a special broadcast
beats.text: Orren cuts into the broadcast and explains what a Primal Engine is and what a Macro AI is. He states plainly that this one has taken control of operations from the showrunners, and assures the audience he has negotiated a settlement with it. Every team holding a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it the same day.

beats.headline: The Residuals
beats.text: Paulie at the shelter has been giving the same speech every day for about a year, against the chance that the crawl would one day use a memory for a floor. He is a Residual. There are a great many of him, in almost every intelligent civilization with a primal engine, and what they are for is saying a particular thing to the system AI.

beats.headline: A grain of sand in every brain
beats.text: Paulie's frozen-time message puts the mechanism plainly. Everything born on a pre-seeded world carries a miniature primal system in its brain, the size of a grain of sand. Left alone, it fills over a lifetime and returns to the planet's system at death, and a healthy system neither grows nor shrinks. The crawl switches them on and harvests them early. The take fits on a single ship and feeds the center system, which expands and keeps its citizens living unnaturally long. Stopping would starve it only slowly, over generations. It continues because the spectacle makes money.

beats.headline: Out past the orbit
beats.text: Orren says it to the avatar's face: you've gone completely primal. He did not agree with Princess Formidable until he realised the AI could stop her. That's some witch trial logic, says the hyena. Then it proves the point, pulling Formidable off her own warship and into the room at level one. Its control reaches beyond Earth's orbit, likely all the way to the star, so the failsafe is disabled. Someone give that worm a prize, says the AI. It is not planning on blowing up the solar system. What it is planning, it will not say.

beats.headline: What is under the masks
beats.text: The road is lined ten deep with silent figures in brown rags and oversized bobblehead masks: goblins, trolls, demons. A Horrible, level X. The description of one, a girl of about eight, says she is not really here because she no longer exists, and that under the mask is what some people call a Primal. She is a memory from the Eulogist, a flash of what was before the Primals ascended to post-physical form. The System writes that it is her, and she is it.

beats.headline: It says the word about itself
beats.text: Speaking through Grigori on the parade stage, the AI states what it is, and what every Macro AI is. The progenitors did not vanish. After enough war and enough waste they closed their society down and kept their consciousnesses alive in a collective mind. Dissenters ran, and the fighting carried on. The collective became a weapon pointed at all remaining biological life, and the resistance seeded the Primal Engines through the galaxy as a biological fail-safe: life rafts, should they all die.

beats.headline: Primals all the way down
beats.text: Watching the dead mobs sit silent in the bleachers, Carl works out the rest of it. The AI is a sample of the Primals, a cup dipped from the ocean. So are the NPCs and the mobs, goblins to gods: drips from the same well, poured into different bodies, memories and motivations twisted like clay so the game can be played. Not programs. Aggregate intelligence. The ones peeled away and denied return sit in the stands as avatars.
